source.title: Cross-Model KV Cache Transfer in LLM Families: A Closed-Form Linear Mapping for Prefill Reuse
source.authors: Taekyung Heo; Rasoul Shafipour; Ritchie Zhao; Maximilian Golub; Mohammad Mahdi Kamani; Ritika Borkar; Makesh Chandran; Pantea Zardoshti; B. Rouhani

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-model representation transfer using a different representation and measure: linear mapping of within-family KV caches followed by downstream evaluation, rather than a general comparison of representation geometries across scale.
record.gate_note: The study measures cross-model KV reconstruction and the usefulness of mapped caches. It does not test a monotonic increase in alignment with scale or cross-modal image-caption alignment. Latency results and cited results from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits closed-form linear (ridge) maps from one model's KV cache to another's within three LLM families. It measures in-sample R2 and the target's downstream accuracy when it decodes from the mapped cache. That is a direct test of V4: whether one model's internal representations can be mapped onto another's with little loss by a simple linear map. It also compares calibration R2 with attention-output cosine as indicators of functional transfer, which bears partly on V6. It does not examine scale trends (V1), cross-modal data (V2), seeds (V3), interpretable features (V5) or causes of alignment (V7).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with corrections. The authors conclude that within-family, matched-KV caches are largely linearly related. A closed-form per-head ridge map retains 73–98% average accuracy on four of six pairs, while two Ministral pairs degrade sharply (42–44%). Retention depends on where residual error lands relative to attention-sensitive subspaces, not its magnitude. Attention-output cosine predicts cross-pair retention better than R2 (+0.57 vs −0.20), and an MLP adds up to +37 pp HellaSwag retention on the failure pairs.
record.recipe_differences: Tests per-head linear KV-cache mapping and downstream cache-transfer performance within matched-KV LLM families; it does not use the original studies' general representation-similarity setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Transfer quality varies substantially by model pair and benchmark. Source-layer count k affects results; the authors report k=1 is uniformly insufficient in their sweep. For Qwen3 14B→32B, removing inference-time RoPE handling sharply lowers some benchmark scores, while a fully RoPE-coupled fit is near the full pipeline on the 1,024-token fit context. Replacing ridge with an MLP improves HellaSwag retention on the two weaker Ministral pairs but slightly reduces it on the two stronger pairs.
record.problems: Evidence is limited to six within-family, matched-KV pairs and does not cover mismatched-KV or cross-family transfer. Calibration uses FineWeb-Edu; k is selected using benchmarks also reported, though the paper measures the selection effect and evaluates additional held-out benchmarks. No uncertainty intervals or significance tests are reported for the main transfer results.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported results were left out. Latency and multi-turn drift results concern serving efficiency and accumulated transfer effects rather than the listed representation-alignment versions.

untested.parts: Cross-family and mismatched-KV pairs; independently trained models with different data or objectives; stitching, relative representations and unpaired mappings. Large-to-small transfer is tested only on HellaSwag.
Geometric similarity measures such as CKA or mutual k-NN, and neighbour-count settings. Domain and input dependence is tested only on one pair.
No test of whether alignment rises with model scale or capability across independently trained models.
No vision-language models or image-caption data.
Causes of alignment (shared data or objectives) and plateaus are not tested; the authors list training-data overlap as future work.

missing.what: Large-to-small HellaSwag retention: Llama 3.1 70B→8B retains only 37%, against 94% small-to-large at the same calibration R2_K=0.84. Ministral 3B↔8B retains 93% in both directions.

Ridge R2 on HellaSwag evaluation tokens. R2_K is 0.75 for Qwen3 14B→32B, −0.10 for Ministral 3B→8B, −7.81 for 3B→14B and −3.22 for 8B→14B, so the calibration-fit map does not extrapolate out of distribution.
Retention on benchmarks never used to select k (PIQA, BoolQ, ARC-Easy). Tier-1 pairs average 96.8–99.9%; tier-2 pairs average 59.3–63.7%.
Calibration-domain dependence on Qwen3 14B→32B. A CodeAlpaca-calibrated mapper loses 5.24 pp on HellaSwag and averages 95.9% across seven benchmarks; Wikipedia averages 99.4%.
Multi-turn CoQA handoff on Qwen3 14B↔32B. Drift is small: the gap widens 1.7 pp over 10 turns small-to-large, and grows 0.33 pp/turn large-to-small.

record.verdict_notes: The record's Table 1 extraction is shifted by columns: values labelled ARC-C through GSM8K were actually Avgfn, ARC-C, HellaSwag, WinoGrande and MMLU. All of r01–r30 were recomputed from Table 13 standalone and transfer accuracies, and match Table 3's HellaSwag ridge values. Tier-2 retention percentages overstate what survives, because accuracies sit at the chance floor; floor-normalized averages are 11–15%. All pairs are same-family models sharing a tokenizer and substantial pretraining data, so this is weak evidence about independently trained models. Tranche could arguably be T3 (new setting: KV caches).

versions.untested_parts: No systematic test of whether alignment rises as models get larger or more capable, or across independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, and data.
No vision-language models or paired images and captions.
No comparison across random seeds of the same architecture, shared features, or shared subspaces.
Tests linear mapping of matched-KV caches within three model families. Does not test stitching, relative representations, unpaired mappings, or general interchangeability of internal representations.
No interpretable features, neurons, circuits, or SAE features are identified or compared.

Compares calibration R2 and attention-output cosine as predictors of downstream retention. Does not comprehensively test geometric similarity measures, neighbour settings, or out-of-distribution inputs as measures of convergence.
Does not test whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment, or whether alignment plateaus. The cache-transfer results are not a direct test of the broader alignment claim.
